Each layer has its own 15 macros. Assign a macro from this layer to each step. Clockwise advances; counterclockwise goes back. Unassigned steps do nothing.

First-time setup & privacy

This editor needs the Kafka firmware installed once. Download firmware for the Keychron Q8 ISO encoder. Later macro edits do not require flashing. It stores texts on the keyboard and drafts in this browser; texts are not sent to a server. Close VIA or Keychron Launcher while using this editor.

Unicode typing on Windows requires WinCompose. In its options, enable Unicode input and keep Right Alt as the Compose key. Accented letters and emoji use more storage bytes than ASCII. Avoid typing or holding Ctrl, Shift, Alt, or Windows while a text plays; a modifier interrupts Unicode playback to prevent accidental shortcuts.

Use a WebHID-capable Chromium browser such as Chrome or Edge, on HTTPS or localhost. On Linux, your user also needs access to the keyboard’s hidraw device. Open the editor as a top-level page if an embedded preview blocks the device chooser.

Saving writes the entire macro library and encoder assignments. An interrupted save disables text playback until a successful retry. Keep a backup before changing firmware or resetting EEPROM. Upgrading from the older shared library changes the storage layout. Export your old library before flashing, then import and save it afterwards. This editor can read/export the previous UTF-8 firmware before the update. FN4 is available for your normal QMK/VIA layer bindings; the site does not activate layers.
